items.title: City Sample gets a major update with PCG and Unreal MCP workflows
items.excerpt: Epic's City Sample project has been rebuilt for Unreal Engine 5.8 with entirely new levels, plus additional toolsets, content and examples for procedural worldbuilding — including PCG and Unreal MCP (agent-driven editor) workflows.
items.rationale: Epic putting agentic MCP + procedural generation inside its canonical reference project is the single most actionable item in the pool — environment artists can open it tomorrow.

items.title: Inworld TTS Open Evaluation Toolkit: Reproducible TTS Evals
items.excerpt: Inworld open-sourced a framework for reproducible text-to-speech evaluation: local ASR, explicit normalization, per-sample measurements and offline reports that can be traced back to the source audio.
items.rationale: An open, reproducible eval harness gives audio directors a defensible way to judge synthetic character voice before it ships — measurement, not vibes.

items.title: 1666: Amsterdam's developer says it 'won't be using any AI anymore', and the tech was only used 'in conception and pre-production'
items.excerpt: Assassin's Creed creator Patrice Desilets says his studio has dropped generative AI from 1666: Amsterdam after backlash, and that the tech had only been used in conception and pre-production — arguably the most creative phase of the whole process.
items.rationale: A named studio publicly reversing gen-AI use, and naming ideation as the phase it touched, is the sharpest fresh data point on where AI is tolerated in a creative pipeline.

items.title: Rockstar is 'at least 10 years ahead' of other games with GTA 6's NPC crowd technology, says dev behind 007 First Light's crowds
items.excerpt: A developer who built the crowd systems in 007 First Light says Rockstar's GTA 6 NPC crowd technology puts it roughly a decade ahead of the rest of the industry, in simulation depth rather than generative shortcuts.
items.rationale: A rival crowd-systems engineer judging the state of the art: systemic hand-built simulation still beats LLM-driven NPC pitches, a useful reality check for anyone budgeting believable characters.

items.title: AI powering the global engine for game studios
items.excerpt: AWS senior gaming solutions architecture manager Huang Zhoubin breaks down how studios are actually operationalising AI — the infrastructure, workflow and production problems that sit between a model demo and a shipped feature.
items.rationale: The unglamorous operational layer — how an AI feature actually reaches a live production pipeline — which is exactly where most studio adoption stalls.
